text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said Slovakia was not considering devaluation of the crown. Meciar said the move would not solve the problem of the worsening trade balace.

- The Association of Security Traders said the move by the OTC bourse RM-System to ban trading with privatisation bonds in cases when the financial settlement was carried out outside the bourse was an adequate reaction to the situation on the market as the rules previous allowed illegal trading.
- The National Property Fund, the state privatisation agency, approved a further 26 privatisation transactions totalling around 667 million crowns.

- Heavy engineering company ZTS Martin, Slovakia's major arms producer, said it planned to increase its production to 2.2 billion crowns this year, from 1.8 billion in 1995, with civilian production accounting for four fifths of overall output. Annual production is planned to total nine billion crowns in the year 2000.

- President Michal Kovac refused to sign the recently approved controversial law on the public prosecutor's office, saying some parts of the law contradicted the constitution. Kovac returned the law to parliament for revision.

PRAVDA - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) is reviewing the stake of security trader ARDS, closely linked to steel producer VSZ, in the bank IRB. NBS is reported to have called for the two companies to reduce their holdings in IRB so that these together do not exceed 15 percent.
- If the NBS finds out that ARDS and VSZ jointly owned more than 15 percent in the bank at its last annual shareholders meeting last August, the results of the AGM will be annulled.
- Tyre producer Matador Puchov said it had cut production plans for its joint-venture in Russian city of Omsk to 170,000 tyres by the end of this year, from the original 200,000 units.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - About half of the Slovak construction companies expect a slowdown in production in October and December.
- The government will discuss long-term production strategy of state-run arms industry coordinator DMD Holding at the end of October.
- Matador Puchov posted turnover of 5.8 billion crowns in the first half of this year, an increase of 20 percent over the same period last year.
